comment: MiniDAQ's tool list (Chapter 20): every tool whose output is in the product (class T3) or is verification evidence (class T2), what a defect in it would do, and why the project trusts it for that use. The classes follow the tool classes of IEC 61508-4 (T1: no effect on the product or the evidence; T2: can fail to reveal a defect; T3: makes part of the product); IEC 62304 asks for the tools to be identified and controlled, not for this scheme. tools/check_tools.py checks the list, writes tools.md and, with --environment, compares the installed versions with the recorded ones. 'shown_to_fail' names a fault of tools/gate_selftest.py, or a test, that shows the tool can report a failure.

tools.name: GCC
tools.use: Compiles the shipped build (preset hardened) and three of the six CI presets.
tools.failure: A miscompiled program that passes its source review.
confidence: Increased confidence from use: the distribution's compiler, used for the whole Ubuntu archive.
Every test runs on the programs it produced, in debug, gcc-cxx23 and hardened builds.
Diverse redundancy: the same tests pass with Clang 18 (clang-release, sanitizers).
The shipped build is reproducible, so a different compiler or a tampered one shows as a different product.

tools.name: Clang and LLVM tools
tools.use: Compiles the clang-release, sanitizer, fuzzing and coverage builds; llvm-cov measures coverage. Not used for the shipped build.
tools.failure: A defect hidden in a verification build; wrong coverage numbers.
confidence: The same tests pass with GCC.
The coverage numbers are cross-checked by Exercise 18.3, whose tests count branches the tool must report.

tools.name: GNU binutils (ld, objcopy, readelf)
tools.use: Links the programs; splits the debug information from the shipped programs; reads ELF properties for the hardening check.
tools.failure: A program linked wrongly or damaged while its debug information is split off.
confidence: The shipped programs are tested after the split (tools/test_release_bundle.py runs them).
tools/release_bundle.py verify checks build IDs and debug links after packaging.

tools.name: CMake and Ninja
tools.version: CMake 3.28 or later, Ninja 1.11 or later
tools.use: Configures and drives the builds; FetchContent fetches the pinned dependencies; CTest runs the tests.
tools.failure: A target built with the wrong flags; a test not run while CTest reports success.
confidence: The hardening check reads the flags from the binaries, not from the CMake files.
The test count of each preset is in the CI log and the release record; the starters must fail (release checks).
The dependencies are pinned by commit and checked against the SOUP list (docs.soup).

tools.name: GoogleTest and GoogleMock
tools.use: Runs the unit, component and property tests of the C++ code.
tools.failure: A failing assertion reported as passed; a test silently not registered.
confidence: Increased confidence from use: one of the most used C++ test frameworks.
Mutation testing shows the tests fail when the code is wrong (Chapter 18).
Every starter must fail at least one test (release checks).

tools.name: Property harness (minidaq/tests/support/property.hpp)
tools.use: Generates inputs and shrinks counterexamples for the property-based tests (ADR 0015).
tools.failure: Generators that never produce the inputs that matter, so a property passes without testing.
confidence: Its own tests: a known-false property must fail and shrink to the minimal counterexample.
Exercise 18.2 shows a uniform generator lets four of eight seeded mistakes survive; the harness's generators find them.

tools.name: Coverage tool (tools/coverage.py)
tools.use: Runs the tests in the coverage build and reports coverage per software item.
tools.failure: Coverage reported higher than reached, so uncovered code escapes review.
confidence: It fails if any test fails, so the report is of a passing run.
Exercise 18.3's solution must pass and its starter fail in the coverage build (release checks).

tools.name: Mutation tool (tools/mutation_test.py)
tools.use: Measures how many planted defects the tests find.
tools.failure: A surviving mutant counted as killed, so weak tests look strong.
confidence: Each survivor of the sorter is argued by hand (sorter-survivors.md); the baseline of the tracker had 7 survivors that the tool reported and new tests killed.

tools.name: clang-tidy and cppcheck
tools.use: Static analysis of the library and the programs (tools/static_analysis.sh).
tools.failure: A finding not reported; files not analyzed.
confidence: The gate self-test plants a finding for each analyzer and checks the gate reports it by name.
Every suppression has a reason in the source (coding standard).

tools.name: Sanitizers (AddressSanitizer, UBSan, ThreadSanitizer)
tools.use: Find memory errors, undefined behavior and data races while the tests run (presets asan-ubsan, tsan).
tools.failure: An error not reported; a build without the sanitizer linked in.
confidence: The gate self-test runs a known heap overflow and a known race and checks both are reported.
The stress run repeats the concurrent tests 100 times under TSan for each release.

tools.name: libFuzzer
tools.use: Fuzzes the parsers and the sorter (CI smoke and 10 minutes per target per release).
tools.failure: Inputs that never reach the code, so a campaign finds nothing.
confidence: Coverage growth is recorded for each campaign; Exercise 7.2 keeps the crash inputs it found in the starter as tests.

tools.name: System test harness and statistics (minidaq/tests/system/)
tools.use: Runs the shipped programs and compares runs with golden data (Chapter 19).
tools.failure: A comparison that cannot fail; a p-value computed wrongly.
confidence: test_stats.py checks the statistics against tabulated values and their calibration.
Negative controls: the impostor servers and the narrower energy window must fail.

tools.name: Test report and soak tools (tools/test_report.py, tools/soak.py)
tools.use: Write the system test report and judge the soak (Chapter 19).
tools.failure: A failed test case reported as passed; a leak judged a pass.
confidence: The report exits with 1 on a failure and marks a dirty tree invalid; the release bundle refuses such a report.
Exercise 19.3 tests the soak analysis on recorded and synthetic series with known faults.

tools.name: Performance gate (tools/perf_gate.py, tools/perf_suite.sh, Google Benchmark 1.9.1)
tools.use: Fails a change that makes a gated benchmark significantly slower.
tools.failure: A regression not reported; noise reported as a regression.
confidence: Exercise 5.3's acceptance tests run against tools/perf_gate.py (test tools.perf_gate).
The gate self-test plants a 20% slowdown; A/A runs measure the false alarm rate.

tools.name: Document checks (tools/trace_matrix.py, req_lint.py, design_file.py, check_*.py, anomalies.py)
tools.use: Check the trace matrix, the requirements' form, document control, SOUP, risk, items, layers, changes and CAPA (CTest docs.*).
tools.failure: An inconsistent regulatory file reported as consistent.
confidence: The gate self-test plants one inconsistency for each of the trace matrix, the requirements, the SOUP list, document control, the layers and the test waits.

tools.name: Hardening check (tools/check_hardening.py)
tools.use: Reads the shipped programs and fails if PIE, RELRO, BIND_NOW, NX or CET is missing.
tools.failure: An unhardened program accepted.
confidence: The gate self-test links a program without PIE and BIND_NOW and checks the tool refuses it.

tools.name: SBOM, Grype and triage (tools/make_sbom.py, Grype 0.120.1, tools/vuln_triage.py)
tools.use: List the SOUP and match it against vulnerability databases (Chapter 17).
tools.failure: A known vulnerability not reported.
confidence: CI scans an SBOM with an old OpenSSL version that has known advisories and fails if Grype finds none.
The SBOM validates against the CycloneDX schema; the triage rules have tests.

tools.name: Simulators and the readout board (minidaq_sim, minidaq_send, the synthetic source)
tools.use: Produce the input and the expected results of verification (Chapters 8, 10, 19).
tools.failure: A model that agrees with a defect, so a test confirms what it should refuse.
confidence: The model card (Chapter 8) states what the simulator models and leaves out; its tests check rates, resolutions and kinematics against analytic values.
minidaq_send reports every fault it injects, and the readout tests account for each (MDQ-PR-018 found and fixed a gap).

tools.name: Release bundle and reproducibility check (tools/release_bundle.py, tools/repro_check.sh)
tools.use: Package the release and its evidence; show that the shipped build is reproducible.
tools.failure: A damaged or mismatched package verified as good.
confidence: tools/test_release_bundle.py damages packages in six ways and checks each is refused.

tools.name: Gate self-test (tools/gate_selftest.py)
tools.use: Shows that the gates above can fail.
tools.failure: A fault planted where the gate does not look, reported as caught.
confidence: Each fault must make the gate fail with output that names the planted fault, and the gate must pass on the unchanged code first.
Its faults are reviewed like tests.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.version: the runner image ubuntu-24.04 of the run
tools.use: Runs the pipeline on every change and keeps its logs.
tools.failure: A job that did not run shown as passed; a changed runner image.
confidence: Every gate also runs locally (ci/run_all.sh, tools/release_checks.sh) on the reference machine for a release.
The tool versions of the runner are checked (tools/check_tools.py --environment).

tools.name: Git
tools.use: Configuration management: every source, test and document is identified by a commit.
tools.failure: A wrong file in a checkout; it would change the commit's hash, so it does not go unnoticed.
confidence: Content addressed: a commit names its exact content.

tools.name: AI coding assistant
tools.version: recorded in each change's commit trailer
tools.use: Proposes code, tests and documents (Part IX).
tools.failure: Plausible code that is wrong, or a test that cannot fail.
confidence: Its output enters the product only through the same review, tests and gates as any other change; it is a source of changes, not a verification tool. Whether the team's procedures allow and record it: assumption: confirm with team.

tools.name: Postmortem tools (tools/postmortem.sh, tools/core_build_id.py, GDB)
tools.version: the commit; GDB as installed (15.1 on the reference machine)
tools.use: Open a core dump of a MiniDAQ program with the matching program and debug information, for the analysis of a problem report (Chapter 21).
tools.failure: A core opened with another build, showing plausible and wrong stacks; a build ID read wrongly from a core.
confidence: tools/test_postmortem.py reads the build ID from a real core and refuses a program and a debug file of another build and a file that is not a core.
The system test of a crash runs the tool on the core of a crashed server where the machine keeps core files.

tools.name: Register map generator (tools/regmap_gen.py)
tools.use: Generates the C++ register definitions of the front-end board, compiled into the server, and their document from hw/feb.toml (Chapter 22).
tools.failure: A register at the wrong address or a field at the wrong bits in the shipped program, or a header that no longer matches its specification.
confidence: tools/test_regmap_gen.py: it refuses unaligned, duplicate and overlapping definitions and reset values outside the fields, and --check fails while an output is out of date.
The test docs.regmap fails while the committed header differs from what the specification generates.
Registers.TheGeneratedMapMatchesItsSpecification and the slow control's tests check the generated types against the specification and the simulated board.

tools.name: Icarus Verilog
tools.version: 12.0 on the reference machine; optional, and not installed on CI
tools.use: Simulates the SystemVerilog listing of the board's output FIFO against its testbench (hw/rtl, test hw.rtl, Chapter 24). The listing teaches; it is not part of MiniDAQ or of the evidence for it.
tools.failure: A wrong listing in the book that the simulation passes; no effect on the product, whose tests use the C++ model of the board.
confidence: The testbench failed on two planted defects of the listing: a clear of the overflow flag that wins over a set, and a push into a full FIFO.

tools.name: Update bundle builder (tools/make_update.py, the OpenSSL command line)
tools.version: the commit; OpenSSL 3.0.13 on the reference machine
tools.use: Builds the archive that is installed into a slot, with its MANIFEST.sha256, and signs the manifest with the release key (Chapter 25).
tools.failure: A bundle whose archive is not the tree that was verified, a MANIFEST.sha256 that vouches for the wrong files, a signature over the wrong bytes.
confidence: tools/test_make_update.py installs bundles it built with minidaq_update, which checks every file against the manifest and the signature independently of the builder.
The same tree gives byte-identical bundles, so a release's bundle can be rebuilt and compared.

tools.name: Platform and unit checks (tools/platform_check.py, tools/check_units.py, systemd-analyze)
tools.version: the commit; systemd-analyze 255 on the reference machine
tools.use: Compare an installed system with the platform definition and write its SBOM; check the systemd units' rules, syntax and exposure (Chapter 25, installation qualification).
tools.failure: An installation that deviates from the platform and passes, or a unit whose hardening was weakened without a failing check.
confidence: tools/test_platform_check.py changes each kind of fact and checks that each gives one named deviation.
check_units.py was run on units with a misspelled directive and an invalid value, and failed on both.

tools.name: Calibration procedure (tools/calib)
tools.version: the commit; Python 3.12 and numpy 1.26 on the reference machine
tools.use: Fit each crystal's photopeak and energy curve and solve each channel's delay from a calibration acquisition, check the acceptance criteria and write the calibration table that minidaq_server applies to every single (Chapter 26).
tools.failure: A table with a wrong gain or delay that passes the acceptance criteria: the server would apply it to every single of every run until the next calibration, shifting energies out of the window or broadening the coincidence timing.
confidence: tools/test_calib.py runs the procedure on a synthetic detector with known gains and delays and checks it finds them; the CRC is checked against the values the server computes.
On minidaq_sim's detector with 10% gain spread, a saturating SiPM and 500 ps delay spread, the gains came out within 0.18% rms and the delays within 21 ps rms of the truth (measurements/ch26).
The server checks every table it loads against its own limits and its CRC (SRS-CAL-001), and the photopeak monitor names a block whose calibration drifted (SRS-CAL-006).

tools.name: Corrections (tools/recon)
tools.version: the commit; Python 3.12 and numpy 1.26 on the reference machine
tools.use: Read MiniDAQ's list-mode files and run records, bin them into sinograms, and compute the normalization, randoms, attenuation, scatter, dead-time and decay corrections that the reconstruction applies (Chapter 27).
tools.failure: A correction that is wrong and looks plausible: the image's values and uniformity would be wrong without an error, in every study corrected with it (H-12).
confidence: tools/test_recon.py checks the reader against files with damaged blocks and headers, the binning against minidaq_listmode's sinograms bin for bin, and each correction on data whose answer is known.

On minidaq_sim's scanner with a 5% efficiency spread and a water phantom, the corrected profile is flat within 1.9% rms against 1.1% for the truth's own noise, and each correction is compared with the simulator's truth (measurements/ch27).
The tool refuses a normalization taken with another energy window, coincidence window, window mode or calibration table (SRS-COR-003).

tools.name: Reconstruction (tools/recon)
tools.version: the commit; Python 3.12 and numpy 1.26 on the reference machine
tools.use: Reconstruct an image from a corrected sinogram: the projector and its adjoint, in numpy and in C++ (recon/, the Python module recon_cpp), MLEM and OSEM with the corrections in the model, and FBP (Chapters 28 to 30); measure the images' figures of merit (Chapter 30).
tools.failure: An image that is not the maximum-likelihood image of the data and looks plausible: activity misplaced, contrast or background biased, or stripes along the gaps, in every image reconstructed with it (H-13).
confidence: tools/test_recon.py checks the dot-product test, the sinusoid of an off-center object, that the likelihood never decreases, that noiseless data give the object back, that unmeasured bins take no part and that the subsets cover the views.

On minidaq_sim's data a point source comes out within 0.3% of its distance from the axis with the lines at 156 mm, and a phantom's background stays flat within 4% from the center to 70 mm with the corrections in the model, against 0.66 to 1.62 without attenuation (measurements/ch28).
Exercises 28.1 to 28.3 each show a mistake of the kind H-13 names failing its tests.

The C++ projector passes the numpy projector's tests through its module (tools/test_recon_cpp.py), agrees with it to 4e-8 forward and 5e-9 back, and has its own tests in recon/tests, run under ThreadSanitizer too (measurements/ch29).

The figures of merit are tested on profiles and images whose answer is known: straight-sided and Gaussian peaks, regions of known levels, FBP of a disc and of a point; Exercises 30.1 to 30.3 each show a mistake in them failing their tests (measurements/ch30).

tools.name: pybind11
tools.use: Generates the conversions between NumPy arrays and C++ of the reconstruction tool's module recon_cpp (Chapter 29).
tools.failure: An array converted wrongly at the boundary (a layout or dtype read as another, a copy that is not made): a projection of the wrong data, in every image reconstructed with the C++ projector (H-13).
confidence: Increased confidence from use: the most used library for C++ extensions of Python, with its own test suite.

tools/test_recon_cpp.py passes the module Fortran-ordered, strided and int32 arrays and compares the results with C-ordered float64 ones bit for bit; the same tests and the line-by-line comparison with the numpy projector run on every build.
Exercise 29.1 shows what the conversion protects against: its starter reads a Fortran-ordered array as rows and fails.

tools.name: Analysis package (analysis/, minidaq-analysis)
tools.version: the commit; the Python environment of analysis/requirements.lock
tools.use: Reads list-mode runs, fits the photopeak and the timing peak, checks the rates and writes the acquisition QC report with the provenance of its inputs (Chapter 31). Its report is evidence that a run, and the detector that took it, meet the QC protocol.
tools.failure: A QC report that passes a run it should fail: a fit whose value or error is wrong, a damaged run read as intact, a lost stretch of data not seen, or a report that cannot be traced to its inputs (H-14).
confidence: Tests against an independent MDQ-L1 writer and against synthetic runs with known faults (a lost stretch, a wrong count, a worse detector, a damaged file); the fits' errors checked by the spread of 300 repeated fits (pulls).
The end-to-end test runs minidaq_sim and finds its detector's resolutions; mypy --strict and ruff run on every push in the CI job python.

tools.name: NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib
tools.use: The arrays, the special functions and statistical distributions, and the figures of the analysis package (TL-33). The other Python tools (TL-29 to TL-31) use the system's numpy.
tools.failure: A wrong number from a library function (an error function, a chi-square tail probability), or a figure that shows other data than the report states.
confidence: Increased confidence from use: the most used numerical libraries in Python, each with its own large test suite.

The analysis package's tests check the results that depend on them against known answers: the area of a bin-integrated Gaussian, the pull distributions, the rejection rate of a constant rate at a stated p-value.

tools.name: pytest, mypy and ruff
tools.use: Run the analysis package's tests, check its types (strict) and lint it, as the CTest tests analysis.pytest, analysis.mypy and analysis.ruff and in the CI job python.
tools.failure: A test that does not run or a failure that is not reported, a type error or a lint finding not shown.
confidence: The CI job requires each of them (MINIDAQ_ANALYSIS_REQUIRED=1): a missing tool fails the job instead of skipping the check.

Each was seen failing on this code while it was written: mypy reported functions returning Any and a dict of the wrong value type, ruff long lines and zip() without strict=, pytest the starters' mistakes.

tools.name: Numba
tools.use: Compiles a Python histogram loop in the measurement of Chapter 31 (measurements/ch31), to compare with numpy and C++. No result of the product or of its verification depends on it.
tools.failure: A wrong time in a comparison in the book.

tools.name: clang-format and git-clang-format
tools.use: Formats C++ as .clang-format says, on the lines a change touches: tools/check_format.py in the pre-commit hook and the CI job format (Chapter 32, ADR 0027).
tools.failure: A line left unformatted or formatted differently: a matter of style. A source change it makes is reviewed, compiled and tested like any other edit, so it cannot reach the product unseen.

tools.name: scikit-build-core
tools.use: Builds the wheel of the reconstruction tool's module recon_cpp from the main CMake project (recon/python/pyproject.toml, Chapter 32).
tools.failure: A wheel that holds another build of the module than the project's (other flags, another source), or that does not hold it: images reconstructed with the wrong projector, as for TL-32 (H-13).
confidence: The wheel is built by the same CMake project and targets as the build tree's module; recon.wheel installs it alone into an empty directory and runs the projector's tests against it, with nothing of the build tree on the path, in the CI job python.
Increased confidence from use: the build backend that the pybind11 and scikit-build projects recommend for CMake extensions.

tools.name: Lock file audit (tools/lock_audit.py)
tools.use: Reports the published vulnerabilities of every package pinned in analysis/requirements.lock, from the Python Package Index's records (SOUP list, section 2); in CI's job python and in the SOUP review of each release.
tools.failure: A pinned package with a published vulnerability reported as clean: a tool of the analysis or of the reconstruction keeps a defect that its supplier has fixed.
confidence: A record without the vulnerability field, or an index that cannot be read, is an error (exit 2), never a clean result.
Its tests use a fake index with a pin that has advisories, one without and one that the index answers without the field.
